chunks: And with this chain of narration,

that a man stayed with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and remained with him for several days. Then he approached him regarding a lawsuit which he did not mention to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he said to him, 'Are you a litigant?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Move away from us, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that a litigant be hosted unless his opponent is with him.'

key_terms.يُضَافَ: To be hosted / entertained as a guest

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hosting a litigant when their opponent is not present?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter on judicial etiquette, this hadith highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) strict adherence to procedural justice by preventing the host from becoming biased toward the guest-litigant. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab al-hukm* (judicial decorum), where the physical presence of the opponent is a prerequisite for a fair hearing to avoid *ghurur* (deception or surprise) and ensure impartiality.
